title: Criterion benchmark suite skeleton for permanent
description:
Add a criterion benchmark suite under `crates/gf2-algebra/benches/permanent.rs` that exercises `permanent_mod3_reference` (T8) and `permanent_bipedal3` (T9) at a defined size sweep, with deterministic seeded inputs.

## Background

Criterion benches are the SSOT for the perf claims. This issue lands the skeleton (size sweep, seeded RNG, Criterion group structure) so that S1 and S6 can extend the existing harness rather than redefine it. The bench targets `permanent_mod3_reference` and `permanent_bipedal3` initially; later issues add SIMD (T12), parallel (T15), F_5 (T18), F_7 (T20) groups.

Default bench sweep $n \in \{8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 28, 32, 36\}$ — 36 is the headline S1 size; smaller sizes give scaling slope. A seeded `StdRng` ensures reproducibility across runs.

## Success Criteria

- [ ] [hard] `crates/gf2-algebra/benches/permanent.rs` exists; `cargo bench -p gf2-algebra` runs end-to-end and produces criterion JSONs under `target/criterion/`.
- [ ] [hard] Two benchmark groups exist: `permanent_mod3_reference` and `permanent_bipedal3`, both swept across $n \in \{8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 28, 32, 36\}$.
- [ ] [hard] Inputs are generated from a fixed seeded `StdRng` so consecutive runs on the same hardware produce reproducible numbers.
- [ ] [hard] Benchmark file uses `Criterion::default().sample_size(...)` tuned so each cell completes in under 60 s on the dev host.
- [ ] [hard] `cargo bench -p gf2-algebra --no-run` succeeds in CI.

## Amendment 2026-05-11 (user-approved, Option A — split sweep ranges)

Original criterion 2 swept both benchmark groups across $n \in \{8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 28, 32, 36\}$, but `permanent_mod3_reference` at $n = 36$ takes 12–30 min per matrix on the dev host (AMD Ryzen 9 5900X), making the cell wall-clock under criterion 4's 60 s/cell budget unachievable for any sample size. The headline 50× speedup comparison at $n = 36$ is delegated to S1's standalone perf criterion; T10's bench groups carry the scaling sweep only.

**Amended criterion 2 (per-group sweep range):**
- `permanent_mod3_reference` group: swept across $n \in \{8, 12, 16, 20, 24\}$ (5 cells). At $n = 24$ the reference is ~8 s/matrix on the dev host; `sample_size = 10` yields ~80 s/cell — borderline under 60 s but the worker may bump to $n_\text{max} = 20$ if the 60 s budget is tight on cold-start runs.
- `permanent_bipedal3` group: swept across $n \in \{8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 28, 32, 36\}$ (8 cells). At $n = 36$ the bipedal path runs ~10–30 s per Gray walk, so each cell with `sample_size = 10` fits the 60 s/cell budget comfortably.

The cross-impl headline 50× number at $n = 36$ (epic criterion 3) is **not** an output of T10; it comes from S1's dedicated perf-criterion bench where the reference $n = 36$ measurement is a separate, single-iteration timing pinned outside the regular bench sweep.

Approved by user 2026-05-11 (epic ae82bd73 session 4, AskUserQuestion option A on T10 sweep amendment).

## Amendment 2026-05-11b (user-approved — Lcg-via-testutil + drop reference n=24)

T10 rework-cycle-1 code review surfaced three findings: (1) the criterion-3 wording "fixed seeded `StdRng`" was paraphrasing — the actual workspace SSOT for deterministic RNG is `gf2_core::rng::Lcg` (already used by every T7/T8/T9/T11 test in this epic); (2) `permanent_mod3_reference` at n=24 with `sample_size = 10` overshoots the 60 s/cell budget per the file's own annotated estimate (~80 s); (3) the bench duplicated `random_matrix_fp3` locally instead of routing through the shared helper.

**Amended criterion 2 (per-group sweep range, reference upper bound trimmed):** `permanent_mod3_reference` group is swept across $n \in \{8, 12, 16, 20\}$ (4 cells). At $n = 20$ the reference is well under the 60 s/cell budget. The dropped $n = 24$ point is computed only as part of S1's headline 50× perf measurement (separate cell, outside this scaling sweep). `permanent_bipedal3` group unchanged: $n \in \{8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 28, 32, 36\}$.

**Amended criterion 3 (RNG SSOT):** Inputs are generated from `gf2_core::rng::Lcg` via `gf2_algebra::testutil::random_matrix::<3>` (the workspace SSOT for deterministic test/bench RNG) with fixed per-cell seeds, so consecutive runs on the same hardware produce reproducible numbers. The original wording named `StdRng`; the workspace standardised on `Lcg` during the 2026-05-10 SSOT consolidation (commit `d6618385` for T7, `fcbaa003` for the shared `crate::testutil` helper). Reasons for choosing `Lcg`: (a) bit-reproducibility across `rand` crate version bumps — `Lcg` is 50 LOC in gf2-core with zero external dependency surface; (b) Charon/Aeneas extractability — the project's Lean4 verification pipeline benefits from a small RNG surface; (c) statistical adequacy — for P ∈ {3, 5, 7} we extract ~1.5 bits per u64, making cryptographic-quality RNG (ChaCha12 in `StdRng`) overkill. The shared helper is exposed via gf2-algebra's `test-support` feature gate following the `gf2-core` workspace pattern.

Approved by user 2026-05-11 (epic ae82bd73 session 4, AskUserQuestion option A on T10 RNG SSOT + sweep trim).

## Amendment 2026-05-11c (user-approved — trim bipedal sweep n=32 + n=36)

T10 rework-cycle-2 code review measured `permanent_bipedal3/36` at ~150 s/call (Criterion estimated 1495 s for 10 samples) and `permanent_bipedal3/32` at ~9.4 s/call (94 s for 10 samples). Criterion's hard minimum `sample_size = 10` means neither cell can fit the criterion-4 60 s/cell budget on the dev host. Dropping both from the scaling sweep.

**Amended criterion 2 (bipedal sweep upper bound):** `permanent_bipedal3` group is swept across $n \in \{8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 28\}$ (6 cells, was 8 cells). At $n = 28$ the bipedal path is ~0.59 s/call on the dev host; 10 samples ≈ 6 s/cell, well inside the 60 s budget. $n = 32$ and $n = 36$ are dropped from this scaling sweep.

The headline 50× speedup measurement at $n = 36$ (epic criterion 3) moves to S1's dedicated perf-criterion cell, which uses a single-iteration timing strategy where multi-hour wall-clock is acceptable. The scaling sweep here remains the SSOT for slope-vs-$n$ analysis at the smaller sizes; the n=36 absolute number is S1's responsibility.

Approved by user 2026-05-11 (epic ae82bd73 session 4, AskUserQuestion option A on T10 sweep trim after rework-cycle-2 measurement).
